1	"""Sub-tree extraction service.
2	
3	Moves a connected branch of an existing tree into a brand-new tree, keeping
4	member ids. The root stays behind in the source tree as the bridge person
5	(tree-in-tree link) with a fresh counterpart seeded in the new tree, and
6	relations crossing the cut elsewhere are severed.
7	
8	The branch is selected by picking a root member and one of two ``direction``
9	values:
10	
11	- ``direct_family`` (default): the root's family of origin — parents,
12	  siblings and their branches, with married-in spouses. The root's own
13	  children never move. See ``_collect_direct_family_ids``.
14	- ``partnership``: the root's partner(s), the partner's family, and the
15	  children the root shares with them. See ``_collect_partnership_ids``.
16	"""
17	
18	from __future__ import annotations
19	
20	from collections import deque
21	from uuid import uuid4
22	
23	from sqlalchemy import select
24	from sqlalchemy.orm import Session
25	
26	from app.api.deps import role_for
27	from app.core.exceptions import (
28	    AccessDeniedError,
29	    ConflictError,
30	    InvalidInputError,
31	    NotFoundError,
32	)
33	from app.db.base import utcnow_iso
34	from app.models import (
35	    Document,
36	    DocumentFile,
37	    DocumentMemberLink,
38	    Event,
39	    EventDocumentLink,
40	    EventMemberLink,
41	    GalleryImage,
42	    GalleryMemberLink,
43	    GalleryUnknownFace,
44	    Member,
45	    MemberDisease,
46	    MemberTask,
47	    Relation,
48	    Story,
49	    StoryDocumentLink,
50	    StoryMemberLink,
51	    Tree,
52	    User,
53	)
54	from app.schemas.extract import SubtreeExtractRequest, SubtreePreview
55	from app.services import feature_service
56	from app.services.activity import record_activity
57	from app.services.cache import invalidate_stats
58	from app.services.event_bus import publish_tree_event
59	from app.services.job_service import ProgressCallback
60	from app.services.merge import _clone_member, _wire_bridge
61	from app.services.storage import (
62	    copy_media_to_tree,
63	    delete_media,
64	    media_disk_usage,
65	    move_media_to_tree,
66	)
67	from app.services.tree_state import mark_tree_opened
68	
69	MemberIdSet = dict[str, set[str]]
70	IdMap = dict[str, str]
71	
72	
73	def _require_readable(db: Session, user: User, tree_id: str) -> Tree:
74	    tree = db.get(Tree, tree_id)
75	    if tree is None or role_for(db, tree, user) is None:
76	        raise NotFoundError("Source tree not found")
77	    return tree
78	
79	
80	def _load_relations(db: Session, tree_id: str) -> list[Relation]:
81	    return list(db.scalars(select(Relation).where(Relation.tree_id == tree_id)))
82	
83	
84	def _pull_one_hop_partners(
85	    relations: list[Relation], moved: set[str], root_id: str
86	) -> None:
87	    """Add, in place, everyone sharing a non-parent (partner-like) relation
88	    with a member already in ``moved`` — a single hop, no further traversal
89	    from the pulled-in members. Partners of the root itself are excluded
90	    (the root is the bridge, never in ``moved``)."""
91	    peers: set[str] = set()
92	    for r in relations:
93	        if r.relation_type == "parent":
94	            continue
95	        if r.from_member_id == root_id or r.to_member_id == root_id:
96	            continue
97	        if r.from_member_id in moved:
98	            peers.add(r.to_member_id)
99	        if r.to_member_id in moved:
100	            peers.add(r.from_member_id)
101	    moved |= peers
102	
103	
104	def _collect_direct_family_ids(
105	    db: Session, tree_id: str, root_id: str
106	) -> set[str]:
107	    """"Direct family" selection: the root's family of origin.
108	
109	    The root R stays as the bridge; R's own children/descendants do NOT
110	    move (they belong to R's partnership in the main tree).
111	
112	    1. Build the vertical (parent-edge) adjacency, traversable both ways.
113	    2. moved = BFS over vertical edges starting from R's PARENTS (rows
114	       where from=R: their to-members), never visiting R itself. This
115	       yields parents, grandparents, siblings (down from parents),
116	       aunts/uncles/cousins (down from higher ancestors) — but never R's
117	       own children, since downward traversal from R never happens (and
118	       any path back down to them passes through R, which is blocked).
119	    3. One-hop partner pull: every member sharing a non-parent relation
120	       with a moved member is added to moved (single hop, no further
121	       traversal) — e.g. a moved brother's wife comes along instead of
122	       being severed. Partners of R itself are NOT pulled.
123	    4. R is excluded from the returned set (it is the bridge).
124	    """
125	    relations = _load_relations(db, tree_id)
126	
127	    vertical: MemberIdSet = {}
128	
129	    def link(a: str, b: str) -> None:
130	        vertical.setdefault(a, set()).add(b)
131	        vertical.setdefault(b, set()).add(a)
132	
133	    root_parents: set[str] = set()
134	    for r in relations:
135	        if r.relation_type != "parent":
136	            continue
137	        link(r.from_member_id, r.to_member_id)
138	        if r.from_member_id == root_id:
139	            root_parents.add(r.to_member_id)
140	
141	    moved: set[str] = set()
142	    queue: deque[str] = deque()
143	    for p in root_parents:
144	        if p not in moved:
145	            moved.add(p)
146	            queue.append(p)
147	    while queue:
148	        node = queue.popleft()
149	        for nb in vertical.get(node, ()):
150	            if nb == root_id or nb in moved:
151	                continue
152	            moved.add(nb)
153	            queue.append(nb)
154	
155	    _pull_one_hop_partners(relations, moved, root_id)
156	    moved.discard(root_id)
157	    return moved
158	
159	
160	def _collect_partnership_ids(
161	    db: Session, tree_id: str, root_id: str
162	) -> set[str]:
163	    """"Partnership" selection: the root's partner(s) and their world, plus
164	    the shared children.
165	
166	    The root R stays as the bridge; the partner side and the shared children
167	    move.
168	
169	    1. seeds = all of R's partners (members sharing any non-parent relation
170	       with R) + all of R's children (parent rows where to=R: their
171	       from-members).
172	    2. moved = BFS from all seeds over ALL edges (vertical + horizontal),
173	       never visiting R.
174	    3. R is excluded from the returned set (it is the bridge).
175	
176	    Deliberately simple: in tangled trees (e.g. two siblings married into
177	    the same family) this can reach back into the root's own blood family —
178	    accepted; the preview's member count reveals it. No cleverness is added
179	    to prevent that (unlike "direct family", which has no such need since it
180	    never leaves the vertical axis until the one-hop partner pull).
181	    """
182	    relations = _load_relations(db, tree_id)
183	
184	    adjacency: MemberIdSet = {}
185	
186	    def link(a: str, b: str) -> None:
187	        adjacency.setdefault(a, set()).add(b)
188	        adjacency.setdefault(b, set()).add(a)
189	
190	    seeds: set[str] = set()
191	    for r in relations:
192	        link(r.from_member_id, r.to_member_id)
193	        if r.relation_type == "parent":
194	            # from = child, to = parent. Root's children: root is the parent.
195	            if r.to_member_id == root_id:
196	                seeds.add(r.from_member_id)
197	        else:
198	            if r.from_member_id == root_id:
199	                seeds.add(r.to_member_id)
200	            elif r.to_member_id == root_id:
201	                seeds.add(r.from_member_id)
202	
203	    moved: set[str] = set()
204	    queue: deque[str] = deque()
205	    for s in seeds:
206	        if s not in moved:
207	            moved.add(s)
208	            queue.append(s)
209	    while queue:
210	        node = queue.popleft()
211	        for nb in adjacency.get(node, ()):
212	            if nb == root_id or nb in moved:
213	                continue
214	            moved.add(nb)
215	            queue.append(nb)
216	
217	    return moved
218	
219	
220	def _collect_member_ids(
221	    db: Session, tree_id: str, root_id: str, direction: str
222	) -> set[str]:
223	    """Return the set of member ids that belong in the sub-tree for ``direction``."""
224	    root = db.scalar(
225	        select(Member).where(Member.tree_id == tree_id, Member.id == root_id)
226	    )
227	    if root is None:
228	        raise NotFoundError("Root member not found in tree")
229	
230	    if direction == "partnership":
231	        return _collect_partnership_ids(db, tree_id, root_id)
232	    return _collect_direct_family_ids(db, tree_id, root_id)
233	
234	
235	def validate_move_request(
236	    db: Session,
237	    user: User,
238	    req: SubtreeExtractRequest,
239	) -> tuple[Tree, Member]:
240	    """Validate an extraction request without writing anything.
241	
242	    Called synchronously from the endpoint before the background job is
243	    created, so precondition failures surface as 4xx responses instead of a
244	    failed job. Returns the source tree and the root (future bridge) member.
245	    """
246	    # direction is a Pydantic Literal, so any value that reaches here is
247	    # already one of the valid choices — no runtime check needed.
248	    # Extraction creates a tree-in-tree link; gate exactly like member subtrees.
249	    if not feature_service.is_enabled(db, "tree_links", user):
250	        raise NotFoundError("Not found")
251	    tree = _require_readable(db, user, req.source_tree_id)
252	    if tree.owner_id != user.id:
253	        raise AccessDeniedError(
254	            "Only the tree owner can extract a branch into a new tree"
255	        )
256	    root = db.scalar(
257	        select(Member).where(
258	            Member.tree_id == tree.id, Member.id == req.root_member_id
259	        )
260	    )
261	    if root is None:
262	        raise NotFoundError("Root member not found in tree")
263	    if root.linked_tree_id is not None:
264	        raise ConflictError("Member is already linked to a tree")
265	    return tree, root
266	
267	
268	def _classify_relations(
269	    relations: list[Relation],
270	    moved: set[str],
271	    root_id: str,
272	) -> tuple[list[Relation], list[Relation], list[Relation]]:
273	    """Split a source tree's relations for a move.
274	
275	    Returns ``(kept, bridged, severed)``:
276	
277	    - kept: both endpoints move → recreated as-is in the new tree,
278	    - bridged: root ↔ moved → recreated with the root replaced by its
279	      counterpart (the bridge person carries the seam),
280	    - severed: moved ↔ anything staying (other than the root) → deleted.
281	
282	    Relations entirely among staying members are not returned (untouched).
283	    """
284	    kept: list[Relation] = []
285	    bridged: list[Relation] = []
286	    severed: list[Relation] = []
287	    for r in relations:
288	        from_moved = r.from_member_id in moved
289	        to_moved = r.to_member_id in moved
290	        if from_moved and to_moved:
291	            kept.append(r)
292	        elif from_moved or to_moved:
293	            other = r.to_member_id if from_moved else r.from_member_id
294	            if other == root_id:
295	                bridged.append(r)
296	            else:
297	                severed.append(r)
298	    return kept, bridged, severed
299	
300	
301	def _split_linked_entities(
302	    links: list,
303	    id_attr: str,
304	    moved: set[str],
305	) -> tuple[set[str], list]:
306	    """Partition member-linked entities (gallery / events / stories) for a move.
307	
308	    An entity whose links ALL point at moved members moves with them; anything
309	    with mixed links stays in the source tree and its links to moved members
310	    are dropped. Returns ``(moved_entity_ids, stale_links_to_delete)``.
311	    Entities without member links never show up here and stay untouched.
312	    """
313	    by_entity: dict[str, list] = {}
314	    for lnk in links:
315	        by_entity.setdefault(getattr(lnk, id_attr), []).append(lnk)
316	    moved_ids: set[str] = set()
317	    stale_links: list = []
318	    for entity_id, entity_links in by_entity.items():
319	        if all(lnk.member_id in moved for lnk in entity_links):
320	            moved_ids.add(entity_id)
321	        else:
322	            stale_links.extend(
323	                lnk for lnk in entity_links if lnk.member_id in moved
324	            )
325	    return moved_ids, stale_links
326	
327	
328	def _load_member_links(db: Session, tree_id: str) -> tuple[list, list, list]:
329	    """All gallery/event/story member links of a tree (link tables carry no
330	    tree_id, so they are reached through their tree-scoped entity)."""
331	    gallery_links = list(
332	        db.scalars(
333	            select(GalleryMemberLink)
334	            .join(GalleryImage, GalleryImage.id == GalleryMemberLink.gallery_image_id)
335	            .where(GalleryImage.tree_id == tree_id)
336	        )
337	    )
338	    event_links = list(
339	        db.scalars(
340	            select(EventMemberLink)
341	            .join(Event, Event.id == EventMemberLink.event_id)
342	            .where(Event.tree_id == tree_id)
343	        )
344	    )
345	    story_links = list(
346	        db.scalars(
347	            select(StoryMemberLink)
348	            .join(Story, Story.id == StoryMemberLink.story_id)
349	            .where(Story.tree_id == tree_id)
350	        )
351	    )
352	    return gallery_links, event_links, story_links
353	
354	
355	def _linked_document_ids(
356	    db: Session,
357	    source_tree_id: str,
358	    *,
359	    moved_member_ids: set[str],
360	    moved_event_ids: set[str],
361	    moved_story_ids: set[str],
362	) -> set[str]:
363	    """Document ids (of ``source_tree_id``) linked to any moving entity.
364	
365	    Documents are reusable, tree-scoped content; a document linked to a member,
366	    event, or story that is relocating must be copied into the new tree so no
367	    link ends up crossing a tree boundary.
368	    """
369	    doc_ids: set[str] = set()
370	    if moved_member_ids:
371	        doc_ids |= set(
372	            db.scalars(
373	                select(DocumentMemberLink.document_id)
374	                .join(Document, Document.id == DocumentMemberLink.document_id)
375	                .where(
376	                    Document.tree_id == source_tree_id,
377	                    DocumentMemberLink.member_id.in_(moved_member_ids),
378	                )
379	            )
380	        )
381	    if moved_event_ids:
382	        doc_ids |= set(
383	            db.scalars(
384	                select(EventDocumentLink.document_id)
385	                .join(Document, Document.id == EventDocumentLink.document_id)
386	                .where(
387	                    Document.tree_id == source_tree_id,
388	                    EventDocumentLink.event_id.in_(moved_event_ids),
389	                )
390	            )
391	        )
392	    if moved_story_ids:
393	        doc_ids |= set(
394	            db.scalars(
395	                select(StoryDocumentLink.document_id)
396	                .join(Document, Document.id == StoryDocumentLink.document_id)
397	                .where(
398	                    Document.tree_id == source_tree_id,
399	                    StoryDocumentLink.story_id.in_(moved_story_ids),
400	                )
401	            )
402	        )
403	    return doc_ids
404	
405	
406	def _copy_documents_for_move(
407	    db: Session,
408	    source_tree: Tree,
409	    new_tree: Tree,
410	    *,
411	    moved_member_ids: set[str],
412	    moved_event_ids: set[str],
413	    moved_story_ids: set[str],
414	) -> None:
415	    """Copy documents linked to moving entities into ``new_tree`` and repoint.
416	
417	    Every document linked (member/event/story) to a relocating entity is copied
418	    — with its files (``copy_media_to_tree`` for ``kind == "file"``) — into the
419	    new tree, and the moving entities' link rows are repointed to the copy. The
420	    original stays behind to serve any links from entities that did not move, so
421	    no link ever crosses a tree boundary.
422	    """
423	    doc_ids = _linked_document_ids(
424	        db,
425	        source_tree.id,
426	        moved_member_ids=moved_member_ids,
427	        moved_event_ids=moved_event_ids,
428	        moved_story_ids=moved_story_ids,
429	    )
430	    if not doc_ids:
431	        return
432	
433	    doc_copy_map: IdMap = {}
434	    for old_doc_id in doc_ids:
435	        doc = db.get(Document, old_doc_id)
436	        if doc is None:
437	            continue
438	        new_doc_id = str(uuid4())
439	        doc_copy_map[old_doc_id] = new_doc_id
440	        db.add(
441	            Document(
442	                id=new_doc_id,
443	                tree_id=new_tree.id,
444	                title=doc.title,
445	                document_date=doc.document_date,
446	                description=doc.description,
447	                created_at=doc.created_at,
448	                updated_at=doc.updated_at,
449	            )
450	        )
451	        for f in db.scalars(
452	            select(DocumentFile).where(DocumentFile.document_id == old_doc_id)
453	        ):
454	            new_url = f.url
455	            if f.kind == "file":
456	                new_url = copy_media_to_tree(f.url, new_tree.id) or f.url
457	            db.add(
458	                DocumentFile(
459	                    id=str(uuid4()),
460	                    tree_id=new_tree.id,
461	                    document_id=new_doc_id,
462	                    kind=f.kind,
463	                    filename=f.filename,
464	                    url=new_url,
465	                    mime_type=f.mime_type,
466	                    size=f.size,
467	                    created_at=f.created_at,
468	                )
469	            )
470	    db.flush()  # copied documents must exist before repointed links reference them
471	
472	    # Repoint the moving entities' link rows to the copied documents. Collect
473	    # the target pairs first, then delete the old rows and add the new ones, so
474	    # the result cursors aren't mutated mid-iteration.
475	    member_links = list(
476	        db.scalars(
477	            select(DocumentMemberLink)
478	            .join(Document, Document.id == DocumentMemberLink.document_id)
479	            .where(
480	                Document.tree_id == source_tree.id,
481	                DocumentMemberLink.member_id.in_(moved_member_ids),
482	            )
483	        )
484	    ) if moved_member_ids else []
485	    event_links = list(
486	        db.scalars(
487	            select(EventDocumentLink)
488	            .join(Document, Document.id == EventDocumentLink.document_id)
489	            .where(
490	                Document.tree_id == source_tree.id,
491	                EventDocumentLink.event_id.in_(moved_event_ids),
492	            )
493	        )
494	    ) if moved_event_ids else []
495	    story_links = list(
496	        db.scalars(
497	            select(StoryDocumentLink)
498	            .join(Document, Document.id == StoryDocumentLink.document_id)
499	            .where(
500	                Document.tree_id == source_tree.id,
501	                StoryDocumentLink.story_id.in_(moved_story_ids),
502	            )
503	        )
504	    ) if moved_story_ids else []
505	
506	    new_member_links = [
507	        (doc_copy_map[link.document_id], link.member_id)
508	        for link in member_links
509	        if link.document_id in doc_copy_map
510	    ]
511	    new_event_links = [
512	        (link.event_id, doc_copy_map[link.document_id])
513	        for link in event_links
514	        if link.document_id in doc_copy_map
515	    ]
516	    new_story_links = [
517	        (link.story_id, doc_copy_map[link.document_id])
518	        for link in story_links
519	        if link.document_id in doc_copy_map
520	    ]
521	    for link in (*member_links, *event_links, *story_links):
522	        if link.document_id in doc_copy_map:
523	            db.delete(link)
524	    db.flush()
525	    for doc_id, member_id in new_member_links:
526	        db.add(DocumentMemberLink(document_id=doc_id, member_id=member_id))
527	    for event_id, doc_id in new_event_links:
528	        db.add(EventDocumentLink(event_id=event_id, document_id=doc_id))
529	    for story_id, doc_id in new_story_links:
530	        db.add(StoryDocumentLink(story_id=story_id, document_id=doc_id))
531	    db.flush()
532	
533	    # Any source document that was linked ONLY to moved entities now has all
534	    # its links repointed to the copy and is left orphaned — clean it up.
535	    _gc_orphaned_documents(db, source_tree.id, set(doc_copy_map))
536	
537	
538	def _gc_orphaned_documents(
539	    db: Session, source_tree_id: str, doc_ids: set[str]
540	) -> None:
541	    """Delete source-tree documents left with no links after a move.
542	
543	    ``doc_ids`` are the documents the move touched (linked to a relocating
544	    entity, hence copied and repointed). A document linked *only* to moved
545	    entities is left with zero member/event/story links once repointing is
546	    done; it would otherwise linger as an orphan in the source tree. Such a
547	    document, its ``DocumentFile`` rows, and the underlying stored files are
548	    removed. Restricting to the touched documents avoids sweeping away
549	    documents the user deliberately left unlinked.
550	    """
551	    for doc_id in doc_ids:
552	        doc = db.get(Document, doc_id)
553	        if doc is None or doc.tree_id != source_tree_id:
554	            continue
555	        has_link = any(
556	            db.scalar(
557	                select(link_model.document_id)
558	                .where(link_model.document_id == doc_id)
559	                .limit(1)
560	            )
561	            is not None
562	            for link_model in (
563	                DocumentMemberLink,
564	                EventDocumentLink,
565	                StoryDocumentLink,
566	            )
567	        )
568	        if has_link:
569	            continue
570	        for f in doc.files:
571	            if f.kind == "file":
572	                delete_media(f.url)
573	        db.delete(doc)
574	    db.flush()
575	
576	
577	def compute_subtree_preview(
578	    db: Session,
579	    user: User,
580	    req: SubtreeExtractRequest,
581	) -> SubtreePreview:
582	    """Preview an extraction without writing anything (same checks as the move)."""
583	    tree, root = validate_move_request(db, user, req)
584	    member_ids = _collect_member_ids(db, tree.id, root.id, req.direction)
585	    moved = member_ids - {root.id}
586	    relations = list(db.scalars(select(Relation).where(Relation.tree_id == tree.id)))
587	    kept, bridged, severed = _classify_relations(relations, moved, root.id)
588	
589	    media_bytes = 0
590	    if moved:
591	        for image_data in db.scalars(
592	            select(Member.image_data).where(
593	                Member.tree_id == tree.id, Member.id.in_(moved)
594	            )
595	        ):
596	            media_bytes += media_disk_usage(image_data)
597	        gallery_links, event_links, story_links = _load_member_links(db, tree.id)
598	        moved_image_ids, _ = _split_linked_entities(
599	            gallery_links, "gallery_image_id", moved
600	        )
601	        if moved_image_ids:
602	            for image_data in db.scalars(
603	                select(GalleryImage.image_data).where(
604	                    GalleryImage.tree_id == tree.id,
605	                    GalleryImage.id.in_(moved_image_ids),
606	                )
607	            ):
608	                media_bytes += media_disk_usage(image_data)
609	        # Documents linked to any moving entity (member, event, or story) are
610	        # copied into the new tree, so their file bytes count toward it.
611	        moved_event_ids, _ = _split_linked_entities(event_links, "event_id", moved)
612	        moved_story_ids, _ = _split_linked_entities(story_links, "story_id", moved)
613	        doc_ids = _linked_document_ids(
614	            db,
615	            tree.id,
616	            moved_member_ids=moved,
617	            moved_event_ids=moved_event_ids,
618	            moved_story_ids=moved_story_ids,
619	        )
620	        if doc_ids:
621	            for url in db.scalars(
622	                select(DocumentFile.url).where(
623	                    DocumentFile.document_id.in_(doc_ids),
624	                    DocumentFile.kind == "file",
625	                )
626	            ):
627	                media_bytes += media_disk_usage(url)
628	
629	    return SubtreePreview(
630	        member_count=len(moved),
631	        relation_count=len(kept) + len(bridged),
632	        severed_relation_count=len(severed),
633	        media_bytes=media_bytes,
634	    )
635	
636	
637	def extract_subtree(
638	    db: Session,
639	    user: User,
640	    req: SubtreeExtractRequest,
641	    progress_cb: ProgressCallback | None = None,
642	) -> Tree:
643	    """Move the selected branch into a new tree linked through the root."""
644	
645	    def _progress(pct: int) -> None:
646	        if progress_cb is not None:
647	            progress_cb(pct)
648	
649	    tree, root = validate_move_request(db, user, req)
650	    member_ids = _collect_member_ids(db, tree.id, root.id, req.direction)
651	    moved = member_ids - {root.id}
652	    if not moved:
653	        raise InvalidInputError(
654	            "Nothing to move: the selection contains only the root member"
655	        )
656	    _progress(10)
657	
658	    new_tree = Tree(
659	        id=str(uuid4()),
660	        name=req.name,
661	        owner_id=user.id,
662	        created_at=utcnow_iso(),
663	    )
664	    db.add(new_tree)
665	    db.flush()
666	    mark_tree_opened(db, new_tree.id, user.id)
667	
668	    # --- Bridge person ---
669	    # The root stays in the source tree; a clone (photo copied, not moved)
670	    # seeds the new tree and the two rows link both ways.
671	    counterpart = _clone_member(root, new_tree.id, str(uuid4()))
672	    counterpart.position_x = 0
673	    counterpart.position_y = 0
674	    counterpart.is_collapsed = False
675	    db.add(counterpart)
676	    db.flush()
677	
678	    _wire_bridge(root, counterpart)
679	    # The branch is gone; the linked-tree badge replaces the collapse chip.
680	    root.is_collapsed = False
681	    _progress(25)
682	
683	    # --- Members: keep ids, re-point the tree, relocate photos on disk ---
684	    for m in db.scalars(
685	        select(Member).where(Member.tree_id == tree.id, Member.id.in_(moved))
686	    ):
687	        m.tree_id = new_tree.id
688	        m.image_data = move_media_to_tree(m.image_data, new_tree.id)
689	        # Zeroed out like the bridge counterpart: all-zero positions mark a
690	        # never-arranged tree, which the frontend auto-lays-out on first open
691	        # rather than opening with stale positions carried over from the
692	        # source tree (which would leave the new tree sparse and disjoint).
693	        m.position_x = 0
694	        m.position_y = 0
695	    _progress(45)
696	
697	    # --- Relations ---
698	    # tree_id is part of the composite PK, so rows are deleted and recreated
699	    # in the new tree rather than mutated in place.
700	    relations = list(db.scalars(select(Relation).where(Relation.tree_id == tree.id)))
701	    kept, bridged, severed = _classify_relations(relations, moved, root.id)
702	    for r in (*kept, *bridged, *severed):
703	        db.delete(r)
704	    db.flush()
705	    for r in kept:
706	        db.add(
707	            Relation(
708	                tree_id=new_tree.id,
709	                from_member_id=r.from_member_id,
710	                to_member_id=r.to_member_id,
711	                relation_type=r.relation_type,
712	            )
713	        )
714	    for r in bridged:
715	        db.add(
716	            Relation(
717	                tree_id=new_tree.id,
718	                from_member_id=(
719	                    counterpart.id if r.from_member_id == root.id else r.from_member_id
720	                ),
721	                to_member_id=(
722	                    counterpart.id if r.to_member_id == root.id else r.to_member_id
723	                ),
724	                relation_type=r.relation_type,
725	            )
726	        )
727	    _progress(60)
728	
729	    # --- Diseases (tree-scoped rows of moved members follow them) ---
730	    for d in db.scalars(select(MemberDisease).where(MemberDisease.tree_id == tree.id)):
731	        if d.member_id in moved:
732	            d.tree_id = new_tree.id
733	
734	    # --- Gallery / events / stories ---
735	    # Entities whose member links ALL point at moved members follow the move
736	    # (ids are stable, so the link rows keep working); entities with mixed
737	    # links stay behind and just drop their links to moved members.
738	    gallery_links, event_links, story_links = _load_member_links(db, tree.id)
739	
740	    moved_image_ids, stale_gallery_links = _split_linked_entities(
741	        gallery_links, "gallery_image_id", moved
742	    )
743	    if moved_image_ids:
744	        for img in db.scalars(
745	            select(GalleryImage).where(
746	                GalleryImage.tree_id == tree.id,
747	                GalleryImage.id.in_(moved_image_ids),
748	            )
749	        ):
750	            img.tree_id = new_tree.id
751	            img.image_data = move_media_to_tree(img.image_data, new_tree.id)
752	        # Unknown-face rows follow their image automatically (they're reached
753	        # only through gallery_image_id, which is unchanged), but the research
754	        # task they created lives in MemberTask, which never moves with this
755	        # extraction. A face whose task is still open here is no longer
756	        # actionable in the source tree, so the task is deleted; a done task is
757	        # kept as history either way. The face's task_id is always cleared so
758	        # it never points at a task in another tree.
759	        moved_faces = list(
760	            db.scalars(
761	                select(GalleryUnknownFace).where(
762	                    GalleryUnknownFace.gallery_image_id.in_(moved_image_ids)
763	                )
764	            )
765	        )
766	        task_ids = {f.task_id for f in moved_faces if f.task_id}
767	        if task_ids:
768	            for task in db.scalars(
769	                select(MemberTask).where(
770	                    MemberTask.id.in_(task_ids),
771	                    MemberTask.tree_id == tree.id,
772	                    MemberTask.done.is_(False),
773	                )
774	            ):
775	                db.delete(task)
776	        for face in moved_faces:
777	            face.task_id = None
778	    for lnk in stale_gallery_links:
779	        db.delete(lnk)
780	    _progress(70)
781	
782	    moved_event_ids, stale_event_links = _split_linked_entities(
783	        event_links, "event_id", moved
784	    )
785	    if moved_event_ids:
786	        for e in db.scalars(
787	            select(Event).where(
788	                Event.tree_id == tree.id, Event.id.in_(moved_event_ids)
789	            )
790	        ):
791	            e.tree_id = new_tree.id
792	    for lnk in stale_event_links:
793	        db.delete(lnk)
794	    _progress(78)
795	
796	    moved_story_ids, stale_story_links = _split_linked_entities(
797	        story_links, "story_id", moved
798	    )
799	    if moved_story_ids:
800	        for s in db.scalars(
801	            select(Story).where(
802	                Story.tree_id == tree.id, Story.id.in_(moved_story_ids)
803	            )
804	        ):
805	            s.tree_id = new_tree.id
806	    for lnk in stale_story_links:
807	        db.delete(lnk)
808	    _progress(84)
809	
810	    # --- Documents ---
811	    # Documents are reusable, tree-scoped content: any document linked to a
812	    # moving member/event/story is copied (with its files) into the new tree
813	    # and the moving entity's link is repointed to the copy, so no link ever
814	    # crosses a tree boundary. The original stays behind for any links from
815	    # entities that did not move.
816	    _copy_documents_for_move(
817	        db,
818	        tree,
819	        new_tree,
820	        moved_member_ids=moved,
821	        moved_event_ids=moved_event_ids,
822	        moved_story_ids=moved_story_ids,
823	    )
824	    _progress(88)
825	
826	    # --- Bookkeeping ---
827	    label = " ".join(filter(None, [root.first_name, root.last_name])) or None
828	    record_activity(
829	        db,
830	        tree_id=tree.id,
831	        actor=user,
832	        action="update",
833	        target_type="member",
834	        target_id=root.id,
835	        target_label=label,
836	        details={
837	            "after": {"linked_tree_id": new_tree.id},
838	            "moved_member_count": len(moved),
839	            "severed_relation_count": len(severed),
840	        },
841	    )
842	    db.commit()
843	    invalidate_stats(tree.id)
844	    publish_tree_event(db, tree, "activity.entry_added", {"tree_id": tree.id})
845	    publish_tree_event(
846	        db, tree, "tree.content_changed", {"tree_id": tree.id, "domain": "member"}
847	    )
848	    db.refresh(new_tree)
849	    _progress(95)
850	    return new_tree
851

"""Sub-tree extraction service.

Moves a connected branch of an existing tree into a brand-new tree, keeping
member ids. The root stays behind in the source tree as the bridge person
(tree-in-tree link) with a fresh counterpart seeded in the new tree, and
relations crossing the cut elsewhere are severed.

The branch is selected by picking a root member and one of two ``direction``
values:

- ``direct_family`` (default): the root's family of origin — parents,
  siblings and their branches, with married-in spouses. The root's own
  children never move. See ``_collect_direct_family_ids``.
- ``partnership``: the root's partner(s), the partner's family, and the
  children the root shares with them. See ``_collect_partnership_ids``.
"""

from __future__ import annotations

from collections import deque
from uuid import uuid4

from sqlalchemy import select
from sqlalchemy.orm import Session

from app.api.deps import role_for
from app.core.exceptions import (
    AccessDeniedError,
    ConflictError,
    InvalidInputError,
    NotFoundError,
)
from app.db.base import utcnow_iso
from app.models import (
    Document,
    DocumentFile,
    DocumentMemberLink,
    Event,
    EventDocumentLink,
    EventMemberLink,
    GalleryImage,
    GalleryMemberLink,
    GalleryUnknownFace,
    Member,
    MemberDisease,
    MemberTask,
    Relation,
    Story,
    StoryDocumentLink,
    StoryMemberLink,
    Tree,
    User,
)
from app.schemas.extract import SubtreeExtractRequest, SubtreePreview
from app.services import feature_service
from app.services.activity import record_activity
from app.services.cache import invalidate_stats
from app.services.event_bus import publish_tree_event
from app.services.job_service import ProgressCallback
from app.services.merge import _clone_member, _wire_bridge
from app.services.storage import (
    copy_media_to_tree,
    delete_media,
    media_disk_usage,
    move_media_to_tree,
)
from app.services.tree_state import mark_tree_opened

MemberIdSet = dict[str, set[str]]
IdMap = dict[str, str]


def _require_readable(db: Session, user: User, tree_id: str) -> Tree:
    tree = db.get(Tree, tree_id)
    if tree is None or role_for(db, tree, user) is None:
        raise NotFoundError("Source tree not found")
    return tree


def _load_relations(db: Session, tree_id: str) -> list[Relation]:
    return list(db.scalars(select(Relation).where(Relation.tree_id == tree_id)))


def _pull_one_hop_partners(
    relations: list[Relation], moved: set[str], root_id: str
) -> None:
    """Add, in place, everyone sharing a non-parent (partner-like) relation
    with a member already in ``moved`` — a single hop, no further traversal
    from the pulled-in members. Partners of the root itself are excluded
    (the root is the bridge, never in ``moved``)."""
    peers: set[str] = set()
    for r in relations:
        if r.relation_type == "parent":
            continue
        if r.from_member_id == root_id or r.to_member_id == root_id:
            continue
        if r.from_member_id in moved:
            peers.add(r.to_member_id)
        if r.to_member_id in moved:
            peers.add(r.from_member_id)
    moved |= peers


def _collect_direct_family_ids(
    db: Session, tree_id: str, root_id: str
) -> set[str]:
    """"Direct family" selection: the root's family of origin.

    The root R stays as the bridge; R's own children/descendants do NOT
    move (they belong to R's partnership in the main tree).

    1. Build the vertical (parent-edge) adjacency, traversable both ways.
    2. moved = BFS over vertical edges starting from R's PARENTS (rows
       where from=R: their to-members), never visiting R itself. This
       yields parents, grandparents, siblings (down from parents),
       aunts/uncles/cousins (down from higher ancestors) — but never R's
       own children, since downward traversal from R never happens (and
       any path back down to them passes through R, which is blocked).
    3. One-hop partner pull: every member sharing a non-parent relation
       with a moved member is added to moved (single hop, no further
       traversal) — e.g. a moved brother's wife comes along instead of
       being severed. Partners of R itself are NOT pulled.
    4. R is excluded from the returned set (it is the bridge).
    """
    relations = _load_relations(db, tree_id)

    vertical: MemberIdSet = {}

    def link(a: str, b: str) -> None:
        vertical.setdefault(a, set()).add(b)
        vertical.setdefault(b, set()).add(a)

    root_parents: set[str] = set()
    for r in relations:
        if r.relation_type != "parent":
            continue
        link(r.from_member_id, r.to_member_id)
        if r.from_member_id == root_id:
            root_parents.add(r.to_member_id)

    moved: set[str] = set()
    queue: deque[str] = deque()
    for p in root_parents:
        if p not in moved:
            moved.add(p)
            queue.append(p)
    while queue:
        node = queue.popleft()
        for nb in vertical.get(node, ()):
            if nb == root_id or nb in moved:
                continue
            moved.add(nb)
            queue.append(nb)

    _pull_one_hop_partners(relations, moved, root_id)
    moved.discard(root_id)
    return moved


def _collect_partnership_ids(
    db: Session, tree_id: str, root_id: str
) -> set[str]:
    """"Partnership" selection: the root's partner(s) and their world, plus
    the shared children.

    The root R stays as the bridge; the partner side and the shared children
    move.

    1. seeds = all of R's partners (members sharing any non-parent relation
       with R) + all of R's children (parent rows where to=R: their
       from-members).
    2. moved = BFS from all seeds over ALL edges (vertical + horizontal),
       never visiting R.
    3. R is excluded from the returned set (it is the bridge).

    Deliberately simple: in tangled trees (e.g. two siblings married into
    the same family) this can reach back into the root's own blood family —
    accepted; the preview's member count reveals it. No cleverness is added
    to prevent that (unlike "direct family", which has no such need since it
    never leaves the vertical axis until the one-hop partner pull).
    """
    relations = _load_relations(db, tree_id)

    adjacency: MemberIdSet = {}

    def link(a: str, b: str) -> None:
        adjacency.setdefault(a, set()).add(b)
        adjacency.setdefault(b, set()).add(a)

    seeds: set[str] = set()
    for r in relations:
        link(r.from_member_id, r.to_member_id)
        if r.relation_type == "parent":
            # from = child, to = parent. Root's children: root is the parent.
            if r.to_member_id == root_id:
                seeds.add(r.from_member_id)
        else:
            if r.from_member_id == root_id:
                seeds.add(r.to_member_id)
            elif r.to_member_id == root_id:
                seeds.add(r.from_member_id)

    moved: set[str] = set()
    queue: deque[str] = deque()
    for s in seeds:
        if s not in moved:
            moved.add(s)
            queue.append(s)
    while queue:
        node = queue.popleft()
        for nb in adjacency.get(node, ()):
            if nb == root_id or nb in moved:
                continue
            moved.add(nb)
            queue.append(nb)

    return moved


def _collect_member_ids(
    db: Session, tree_id: str, root_id: str, direction: str
) -> set[str]:
    """Return the set of member ids that belong in the sub-tree for ``direction``."""
    root = db.scalar(
        select(Member).where(Member.tree_id == tree_id, Member.id == root_id)
    )
    if root is None:
        raise NotFoundError("Root member not found in tree")

    if direction == "partnership":
        return _collect_partnership_ids(db, tree_id, root_id)
    return _collect_direct_family_ids(db, tree_id, root_id)


def validate_move_request(
    db: Session,
    user: User,
    req: SubtreeExtractRequest,
) -> tuple[Tree, Member]:
    """Validate an extraction request without writing anything.

    Called synchronously from the endpoint before the background job is
    created, so precondition failures surface as 4xx responses instead of a
    failed job. Returns the source tree and the root (future bridge) member.
    """
    # direction is a Pydantic Literal, so any value that reaches here is
    # already one of the valid choices — no runtime check needed.
    # Extraction creates a tree-in-tree link; gate exactly like member subtrees.
    if not feature_service.is_enabled(db, "tree_links", user):
        raise NotFoundError("Not found")
    tree = _require_readable(db, user, req.source_tree_id)
    if tree.owner_id != user.id:
        raise AccessDeniedError(
            "Only the tree owner can extract a branch into a new tree"
        )
    root = db.scalar(
        select(Member).where(
            Member.tree_id == tree.id, Member.id == req.root_member_id
        )
    )
    if root is None:
        raise NotFoundError("Root member not found in tree")
    if root.linked_tree_id is not None:
        raise ConflictError("Member is already linked to a tree")
    return tree, root


def _classify_relations(
    relations: list[Relation],
    moved: set[str],
    root_id: str,
) -> tuple[list[Relation], list[Relation], list[Relation]]:
    """Split a source tree's relations for a move.

    Returns ``(kept, bridged, severed)``:

    - kept: both endpoints move → recreated as-is in the new tree,
    - bridged: root ↔ moved → recreated with the root replaced by its
      counterpart (the bridge person carries the seam),
    - severed: moved ↔ anything staying (other than the root) → deleted.

    Relations entirely among staying members are not returned (untouched).
    """
    kept: list[Relation] = []
    bridged: list[Relation] = []
    severed: list[Relation] = []
    for r in relations:
        from_moved = r.from_member_id in moved
        to_moved = r.to_member_id in moved
        if from_moved and to_moved:
            kept.append(r)
        elif from_moved or to_moved:
            other = r.to_member_id if from_moved else r.from_member_id
            if other == root_id:
                bridged.append(r)
            else:
                severed.append(r)
    return kept, bridged, severed


def _split_linked_entities(
    links: list,
    id_attr: str,
    moved: set[str],
) -> tuple[set[str], list]:
    """Partition member-linked entities (gallery / events / stories) for a move.

    An entity whose links ALL point at moved members moves with them; anything
    with mixed links stays in the source tree and its links to moved members
    are dropped. Returns ``(moved_entity_ids, stale_links_to_delete)``.
    Entities without member links never show up here and stay untouched.
    """
    by_entity: dict[str, list] = {}
    for lnk in links:
        by_entity.setdefault(getattr(lnk, id_attr), []).append(lnk)
    moved_ids: set[str] = set()
    stale_links: list = []
    for entity_id, entity_links in by_entity.items():
        if all(lnk.member_id in moved for lnk in entity_links):
            moved_ids.add(entity_id)
        else:
            stale_links.extend(
                lnk for lnk in entity_links if lnk.member_id in moved
            )
    return moved_ids, stale_links


def _load_member_links(db: Session, tree_id: str) -> tuple[list, list, list]:
    """All gallery/event/story member links of a tree (link tables carry no
    tree_id, so they are reached through their tree-scoped entity)."""
    gallery_links = list(
        db.scalars(
            select(GalleryMemberLink)
            .join(GalleryImage, GalleryImage.id == GalleryMemberLink.gallery_image_id)
            .where(GalleryImage.tree_id == tree_id)
        )
    )
    event_links = list(
        db.scalars(
            select(EventMemberLink)
            .join(Event, Event.id == EventMemberLink.event_id)
            .where(Event.tree_id == tree_id)
        )
    )
    story_links = list(
        db.scalars(
            select(StoryMemberLink)
            .join(Story, Story.id == StoryMemberLink.story_id)
            .where(Story.tree_id == tree_id)
        )
    )
    return gallery_links, event_links, story_links


def _linked_document_ids(
    db: Session,
    source_tree_id: str,
    *,
    moved_member_ids: set[str],
    moved_event_ids: set[str],
    moved_story_ids: set[str],
) -> set[str]:
    """Document ids (of ``source_tree_id``) linked to any moving entity.

    Documents are reusable, tree-scoped content; a document linked to a member,
    event, or story that is relocating must be copied into the new tree so no
    link ends up crossing a tree boundary.
    """
    doc_ids: set[str] = set()
    if moved_member_ids:
        doc_ids |= set(
            db.scalars(
                select(DocumentMemberLink.document_id)
                .join(Document, Document.id == DocumentMemberLink.document_id)
                .where(
                    Document.tree_id == source_tree_id,
                    DocumentMemberLink.member_id.in_(moved_member_ids),
                )
            )
        )
    if moved_event_ids:
        doc_ids |= set(
            db.scalars(
                select(EventDocumentLink.document_id)
                .join(Document, Document.id == EventDocumentLink.document_id)
                .where(
                    Document.tree_id == source_tree_id,
                    EventDocumentLink.event_id.in_(moved_event_ids),
                )
            )
        )
    if moved_story_ids:
        doc_ids |= set(
            db.scalars(
                select(StoryDocumentLink.document_id)
                .join(Document, Document.id == StoryDocumentLink.document_id)
                .where(
                    Document.tree_id == source_tree_id,
                    StoryDocumentLink.story_id.in_(moved_story_ids),
                )
            )
        )
    return doc_ids


def _copy_documents_for_move(
    db: Session,
    source_tree: Tree,
    new_tree: Tree,
    *,
    moved_member_ids: set[str],
    moved_event_ids: set[str],
    moved_story_ids: set[str],
) -> None:
    """Copy documents linked to moving entities into ``new_tree`` and repoint.

    Every document linked (member/event/story) to a relocating entity is copied
    — with its files (``copy_media_to_tree`` for ``kind == "file"``) — into the
    new tree, and the moving entities' link rows are repointed to the copy. The
    original stays behind to serve any links from entities that did not move, so
    no link ever crosses a tree boundary.
    """
    doc_ids = _linked_document_ids(
        db,
        source_tree.id,
        moved_member_ids=moved_member_ids,
        moved_event_ids=moved_event_ids,
        moved_story_ids=moved_story_ids,
    )
    if not doc_ids:
        return

    doc_copy_map: IdMap = {}
    for old_doc_id in doc_ids:
        doc = db.get(Document, old_doc_id)
        if doc is None:
            continue
        new_doc_id = str(uuid4())
        doc_copy_map[old_doc_id] = new_doc_id
        db.add(
            Document(
                id=new_doc_id,
                tree_id=new_tree.id,
                title=doc.title,
                document_date=doc.document_date,
                description=doc.description,
                created_at=doc.created_at,
                updated_at=doc.updated_at,
            )
        )
        for f in db.scalars(
            select(DocumentFile).where(DocumentFile.document_id == old_doc_id)
        ):
            new_url = f.url
            if f.kind == "file":
                new_url = copy_media_to_tree(f.url, new_tree.id) or f.url
            db.add(
                DocumentFile(
                    id=str(uuid4()),
                    tree_id=new_tree.id,
                    document_id=new_doc_id,
                    kind=f.kind,
                    filename=f.filename,
                    url=new_url,
                    mime_type=f.mime_type,
                    size=f.size,
                    created_at=f.created_at,
                )
            )
    db.flush()  # copied documents must exist before repointed links reference them

    # Repoint the moving entities' link rows to the copied documents. Collect
    # the target pairs first, then delete the old rows and add the new ones, so
    # the result cursors aren't mutated mid-iteration.
    member_links = list(
        db.scalars(
            select(DocumentMemberLink)
            .join(Document, Document.id == DocumentMemberLink.document_id)
            .where(
                Document.tree_id == source_tree.id,
                DocumentMemberLink.member_id.in_(moved_member_ids),
            )
        )
    ) if moved_member_ids else []
    event_links = list(
        db.scalars(
            select(EventDocumentLink)
            .join(Document, Document.id == EventDocumentLink.document_id)
            .where(
                Document.tree_id == source_tree.id,
                EventDocumentLink.event_id.in_(moved_event_ids),
            )
        )
    ) if moved_event_ids else []
    story_links = list(
        db.scalars(
            select(StoryDocumentLink)
            .join(Document, Document.id == StoryDocumentLink.document_id)
            .where(
                Document.tree_id == source_tree.id,
                StoryDocumentLink.story_id.in_(moved_story_ids),
            )
        )
    ) if moved_story_ids else []

    new_member_links = [
        (doc_copy_map[link.document_id], link.member_id)
        for link in member_links
        if link.document_id in doc_copy_map
    ]
    new_event_links = [
        (link.event_id, doc_copy_map[link.document_id])
        for link in event_links
        if link.document_id in doc_copy_map
    ]
    new_story_links = [
        (link.story_id, doc_copy_map[link.document_id])
        for link in story_links
        if link.document_id in doc_copy_map
    ]
    for link in (*member_links, *event_links, *story_links):
        if link.document_id in doc_copy_map:
            db.delete(link)
    db.flush()
    for doc_id, member_id in new_member_links:
        db.add(DocumentMemberLink(document_id=doc_id, member_id=member_id))
    for event_id, doc_id in new_event_links:
        db.add(EventDocumentLink(event_id=event_id, document_id=doc_id))
    for story_id, doc_id in new_story_links:
        db.add(StoryDocumentLink(story_id=story_id, document_id=doc_id))
    db.flush()

    # Any source document that was linked ONLY to moved entities now has all
    # its links repointed to the copy and is left orphaned — clean it up.
    _gc_orphaned_documents(db, source_tree.id, set(doc_copy_map))


def _gc_orphaned_documents(
    db: Session, source_tree_id: str, doc_ids: set[str]
) -> None:
    """Delete source-tree documents left with no links after a move.

    ``doc_ids`` are the documents the move touched (linked to a relocating
    entity, hence copied and repointed). A document linked *only* to moved
    entities is left with zero member/event/story links once repointing is
    done; it would otherwise linger as an orphan in the source tree. Such a
    document, its ``DocumentFile`` rows, and the underlying stored files are
    removed. Restricting to the touched documents avoids sweeping away
    documents the user deliberately left unlinked.
    """
    for doc_id in doc_ids:
        doc = db.get(Document, doc_id)
        if doc is None or doc.tree_id != source_tree_id:
            continue
        has_link = any(
            db.scalar(
                select(link_model.document_id)
                .where(link_model.document_id == doc_id)
                .limit(1)
            )
            is not None
            for link_model in (
                DocumentMemberLink,
                EventDocumentLink,
                StoryDocumentLink,
            )
        )
        if has_link:
            continue
        for f in doc.files:
            if f.kind == "file":
                delete_media(f.url)
        db.delete(doc)
    db.flush()


def compute_subtree_preview(
    db: Session,
    user: User,
    req: SubtreeExtractRequest,
) -> SubtreePreview:
    """Preview an extraction without writing anything (same checks as the move)."""
    tree, root = validate_move_request(db, user, req)
    member_ids = _collect_member_ids(db, tree.id, root.id, req.direction)
    moved = member_ids - {root.id}
    relations = list(db.scalars(select(Relation).where(Relation.tree_id == tree.id)))
    kept, bridged, severed = _classify_relations(relations, moved, root.id)

    media_bytes = 0
    if moved:
        for image_data in db.scalars(
            select(Member.image_data).where(
                Member.tree_id == tree.id, Member.id.in_(moved)
            )
        ):
            media_bytes += media_disk_usage(image_data)
        gallery_links, event_links, story_links = _load_member_links(db, tree.id)
        moved_image_ids, _ = _split_linked_entities(
            gallery_links, "gallery_image_id", moved
        )
        if moved_image_ids:
            for image_data in db.scalars(
                select(GalleryImage.image_data).where(
                    GalleryImage.tree_id == tree.id,
                    GalleryImage.id.in_(moved_image_ids),
                )
            ):
                media_bytes += media_disk_usage(image_data)
        # Documents linked to any moving entity (member, event, or story) are
        # copied into the new tree, so their file bytes count toward it.
        moved_event_ids, _ = _split_linked_entities(event_links, "event_id", moved)
        moved_story_ids, _ = _split_linked_entities(story_links, "story_id", moved)
        doc_ids = _linked_document_ids(
            db,
            tree.id,
            moved_member_ids=moved,
            moved_event_ids=moved_event_ids,
            moved_story_ids=moved_story_ids,
        )
        if doc_ids:
            for url in db.scalars(
                select(DocumentFile.url).where(
                    DocumentFile.document_id.in_(doc_ids),
                    DocumentFile.kind == "file",
                )
            ):
                media_bytes += media_disk_usage(url)

    return SubtreePreview(
        member_count=len(moved),
        relation_count=len(kept) + len(bridged),
        severed_relation_count=len(severed),
        media_bytes=media_bytes,
    )


def extract_subtree(
    db: Session,
    user: User,
    req: SubtreeExtractRequest,
    progress_cb: ProgressCallback | None = None,
) -> Tree:
    """Move the selected branch into a new tree linked through the root."""

    def _progress(pct: int) -> None:
        if progress_cb is not None:
            progress_cb(pct)

    tree, root = validate_move_request(db, user, req)
    member_ids = _collect_member_ids(db, tree.id, root.id, req.direction)
    moved = member_ids - {root.id}
    if not moved:
        raise InvalidInputError(
            "Nothing to move: the selection contains only the root member"
        )
    _progress(10)

    new_tree = Tree(
        id=str(uuid4()),
        name=req.name,
        owner_id=user.id,
        created_at=utcnow_iso(),
    )
    db.add(new_tree)
    db.flush()
    mark_tree_opened(db, new_tree.id, user.id)

    # --- Bridge person ---
    # The root stays in the source tree; a clone (photo copied, not moved)
    # seeds the new tree and the two rows link both ways.
    counterpart = _clone_member(root, new_tree.id, str(uuid4()))
    counterpart.position_x = 0
    counterpart.position_y = 0
    counterpart.is_collapsed = False
    db.add(counterpart)
    db.flush()

    _wire_bridge(root, counterpart)
    # The branch is gone; the linked-tree badge replaces the collapse chip.
    root.is_collapsed = False
    _progress(25)

    # --- Members: keep ids, re-point the tree, relocate photos on disk ---
    for m in db.scalars(
        select(Member).where(Member.tree_id == tree.id, Member.id.in_(moved))
    ):
        m.tree_id = new_tree.id
        m.image_data = move_media_to_tree(m.image_data, new_tree.id)
        # Zeroed out like the bridge counterpart: all-zero positions mark a
        # never-arranged tree, which the frontend auto-lays-out on first open
        # rather than opening with stale positions carried over from the
        # source tree (which would leave the new tree sparse and disjoint).
        m.position_x = 0
        m.position_y = 0
    _progress(45)

    # --- Relations ---
    # tree_id is part of the composite PK, so rows are deleted and recreated
    # in the new tree rather than mutated in place.
    relations = list(db.scalars(select(Relation).where(Relation.tree_id == tree.id)))
    kept, bridged, severed = _classify_relations(relations, moved, root.id)
    for r in (*kept, *bridged, *severed):
        db.delete(r)
    db.flush()
    for r in kept:
        db.add(
            Relation(
                tree_id=new_tree.id,
                from_member_id=r.from_member_id,
                to_member_id=r.to_member_id,
                relation_type=r.relation_type,
            )
        )
    for r in bridged:
        db.add(
            Relation(
                tree_id=new_tree.id,
                from_member_id=(
                    counterpart.id if r.from_member_id == root.id else r.from_member_id
                ),
                to_member_id=(
                    counterpart.id if r.to_member_id == root.id else r.to_member_id
                ),
                relation_type=r.relation_type,
            )
        )
    _progress(60)

    # --- Diseases (tree-scoped rows of moved members follow them) ---
    for d in db.scalars(select(MemberDisease).where(MemberDisease.tree_id == tree.id)):
        if d.member_id in moved:
            d.tree_id = new_tree.id

    # --- Gallery / events / stories ---
    # Entities whose member links ALL point at moved members follow the move
    # (ids are stable, so the link rows keep working); entities with mixed
    # links stay behind and just drop their links to moved members.
    gallery_links, event_links, story_links = _load_member_links(db, tree.id)

    moved_image_ids, stale_gallery_links = _split_linked_entities(
        gallery_links, "gallery_image_id", moved
    )
    if moved_image_ids:
        for img in db.scalars(
            select(GalleryImage).where(
                GalleryImage.tree_id == tree.id,
                GalleryImage.id.in_(moved_image_ids),
            )
        ):
            img.tree_id = new_tree.id
            img.image_data = move_media_to_tree(img.image_data, new_tree.id)
        # Unknown-face rows follow their image automatically (they're reached
        # only through gallery_image_id, which is unchanged), but the research
        # task they created lives in MemberTask, which never moves with this
        # extraction. A face whose task is still open here is no longer
        # actionable in the source tree, so the task is deleted; a done task is
        # kept as history either way. The face's task_id is always cleared so
        # it never points at a task in another tree.
        moved_faces = list(
            db.scalars(
                select(GalleryUnknownFace).where(
                    GalleryUnknownFace.gallery_image_id.in_(moved_image_ids)
                )
            )
        )
        task_ids = {f.task_id for f in moved_faces if f.task_id}
        if task_ids:
            for task in db.scalars(
                select(MemberTask).where(
                    MemberTask.id.in_(task_ids),

    for lnk in stale_gallery_links:

    _progress(70)

    moved_event_ids, stale_event_links = _split_linked_entities(
        event_links, "event_id", moved
    )
    if moved_event_ids:
        for e in db.scalars(
            select(Event).where(
                Event.tree_id == tree.id, Event.id.in_(moved_event_ids)
            )
        ):

    for lnk in stale_event_links:

    _progress(78)

    moved_story_ids, stale_story_links = _split_linked_entities(
        story_links, "story_id", moved

    # --- Documents ---

    _progress(88)

    # --- Bookkeeping ---
    label = " ".join(filter(None, [root.first_name, root.last_name])) or None
    record_activity(
        db,
        tree_id=tree.id,
        actor=user,
        action="update",
        target_type="member",
        target_id=root.id,
        target_label=label,
        details={

        db, tree, "tree.content_changed", {"tree_id": tree.id, "domain": "member"}
    )
    db.refresh(new_tree)
    _progress(95)
    return new_tree

"""Single-owner transaction boundary for application commands.

A mutation typically has to: write its rows, record an activity-log entry in
the same transaction, commit, and only then publish SSE events / invalidate
caches. Hand-assembling that sequence in every route makes it easy to publish
before a commit (or after one that failed) or to skip a step. ``UnitOfWork``
makes the ordering structural instead of conventional: side effects queued
with ``after_commit`` cannot run unless the wrapped commit actually succeeds.

Usage::

    with UnitOfWork(db) as uow:
        db.add(story)
        record_activity(db, tree_id=tree.id, actor=user, action="create", ...)
        uow.after_commit(lambda: publish_tree_event(db, tree, "entry_added", ...))
        uow.after_commit(lambda: publish_tree_event(db, tree, "content_changed", ...))

On a clean exit the session is committed and the queued callbacks run, in
order. On an exception raised inside the block — or by the commit itself —
the session is rolled back, the callbacks are discarded, and the exception
propagates: an event can never be published, nor a cache key invalidated,
for a mutation that didn't land.
"""

from __future__ import annotations

from collections.abc import Callable
from types import TracebackType

from sqlalchemy.orm import Session


class UnitOfWork:
    def __init__(self, db: Session) -> None:
        self._db = db
        self._callbacks: list[Callable[[], None]] = []

    def after_commit(self, callback: Callable[[], None]) -> None:
        """Queue *callback* to run once this unit of work commits successfully."""
        self._callbacks.append(callback)

    def __enter__(self) -> UnitOfWork:
        return self

    def __exit__(
        self,
        exc_type: type[BaseException] | None,
        exc: BaseException | None,
        tb: TracebackType | None,
    ) -> None:
        if exc_type is not None:
            self._db.rollback()
            self._callbacks.clear()
            return
        try:
            self._db.commit()
        except BaseException:
            self._db.rollback()
            self._callbacks.clear()
            raise
        # Drain before running: a callback that re-enters this UnitOfWork
        # (or an instance reused for a later mutation) must never replay
        # callbacks queued by this commit.
        callbacks, self._callbacks = self._callbacks, []
        for callback in callbacks:
            callback()

463	def _do_import(
464	    progress_cb: ProgressCallback,
465	    bundle: TreeBundleV4,
466	    name: str | None,
467	    user_id: str,
468	) -> str:
469	    """Run the full bundle import in a background thread; return new tree_id."""
470	    progress_cb(5)
471	    # bundle is already decrypted and validated by the route handler.
472	    progress_cb(10)
473	
474	    db = SessionLocal()
475	    tree_id: str | None = None
476	    try:
477	        tree = Tree(
478	            id=str(uuid4()),
479	            name=name or bundle.get("tree", {}).get("name") or "Imported tree",
480	            owner_id=user_id,
481	            created_at=utcnow_iso(),
482	        )
483	        db.add(tree)
484	        db.flush()
485	        mark_tree_opened(db, tree.id, user_id)
486	        tree_id = tree.id
487	        progress_cb(15)
488	
489	        media_limits = get_media_limits(db)
490	        members = bundle.get("members", [])
491	        member_map = _remap(members)
492	        total_members = max(len(members), 1)
493	
494	        # Build per-row member dicts (image processing must stay per-row), then
495	        # bulk-insert in chunks for performance on large imports.
496	        member_dicts: list[dict] = []
497	        for i, row in enumerate(members):
498	            data = dict(row)
499	            data.pop("tree_id", None)
500	            data["id"] = member_map[row["id"]]
501	            data["tree_id"] = tree.id
502	            data["image_data"] = process_image_field(
503	                tree.id, data.get("image_data"), media_limits
504	            )
505	            # Older bundles may not include the sort columns; compute if missing.
506	            if data.get("date_of_birth_sort") is None:
507	                data["date_of_birth_sort"] = _sort_key(data.get("date_of_birth"))
508	            if data.get("date_of_death_sort") is None:
509	                data["date_of_death_sort"] = _sort_key(data.get("date_of_death"))
510	            member_dicts.append(data)
511	
512	            if i % _BULK_CHUNK == 0:
513	                progress_cb(15 + int(40 * i / total_members))
514	
515	        _bulk_insert_chunked(db, Member, member_dicts)
516	        db.flush()
517	        progress_cb(55)
518	
519	        known_types = set(db.scalars(select(RelationType.id)).all())
520	        for row in bundle.get("relation_types", []):
521	            if row["id"] not in known_types:
522	                known_types.add(row["id"])
523	                db.add(RelationType(id=row["id"], description=row.get("description")))
524	
525	        relation_dicts: list[dict] = [
526	            {
527	                "tree_id": tree.id,
528	                "from_member_id": member_map[row["from_member_id"]],
529	                "to_member_id": member_map[row["to_member_id"]],
530	                "relation_type": row["relation_type"],
531	            }
532	            for row in bundle.get("relations", [])
533	            if row["from_member_id"] in member_map and row["to_member_id"] in member_map
534	        ]
535	        _bulk_insert_chunked(db, Relation, relation_dicts)
536	
537	        for row in bundle.get("diseases", []):
538	            data = dict(row)
539	            data.pop("tree_id", None)
540	            data["id"] = str(uuid4())
541	            data["member_id"] = member_map.get(row["member_id"], row["member_id"])
542	            if data["member_id"] in member_map.values():
543	                db.add(MemberDisease(tree_id=tree.id, **data))
544	
545	        task_map = _remap(bundle.get("tasks", []))
546	        for row in bundle.get("tasks", []):
547	            data = dict(row)
548	            data.pop("tree_id", None)
549	            data["id"] = task_map[row["id"]]
550	            db.add(MemberTask(tree_id=tree.id, **data))
551	        _import_links(db, bundle.get("task_links", []), MemberTaskLink,
552	                      "task_id", task_map, member_map)
553	        progress_cb(65)
554	
555	        gallery_map = _remap(bundle.get("gallery_images", []))
556	        for row in bundle.get("gallery_images", []):
557	            data = dict(row)
558	            data.pop("tree_id", None)
559	            data["id"] = gallery_map[row["id"]]
560	            data["image_data"] = process_image_field(
561	                tree.id, data.get("image_data"), media_limits
562	            )
563	            db.add(GalleryImage(tree_id=tree.id, **data))
564	        _import_links(db, bundle.get("gallery_links", []), GalleryMemberLink,
565	                      "gallery_image_id", gallery_map, member_map)
566	        _import_unknown_faces(
567	            db, bundle.get("unknown_faces", []), gallery_map, task_map
568	        )
569	        progress_cb(72)
570	
571	        event_map = _remap(bundle.get("events", []))
572	        for row in bundle.get("events", []):
573	            data = dict(row)
574	            data.pop("tree_id", None)
575	            data["id"] = event_map[row["id"]]
576	            db.add(Event(tree_id=tree.id, **data))
577	        _import_links(db, bundle.get("event_links", []), EventMemberLink,
578	                      "event_id", event_map, member_map)
579	        progress_cb(79)
580	
581	        story_map = _remap(bundle.get("stories", []))
582	        for row in bundle.get("stories", []):
583	            data = dict(row)
584	            data.pop("tree_id", None)
585	            data["id"] = story_map[row["id"]]
586	            db.add(Story(tree_id=tree.id, **data))
587	        _import_links(db, bundle.get("story_links", []), StoryMemberLink,
588	                      "story_id", story_map, member_map)
589	        db.flush()
590	        progress_cb(84)
591	
592	        document_map = _remap(bundle.get("documents", []))
593	        for row in bundle.get("documents", []):
594	            data = dict(row)
595	            data.pop("tree_id", None)
596	            data["id"] = document_map[row["id"]]
597	            db.add(Document(tree_id=tree.id, **data))
598	        db.flush()  # documents before their files/links
599	
600	        for row in bundle.get("document_files", []):
601	            document_id = document_map.get(row.get("document_id"))
602	            if document_id is None:
603	                continue
604	            file_url = row.get("url", "")
605	            file_mime = row.get("mime_type")
606	            file_size = row.get("size")
607	            if row.get("kind") == "file":
608	                try:
609	                    file_url, file_mime, file_size = store_document(
610	                        tree.id, row.get("filename") or "file", file_url, media_limits,
611	                    )
612	                except ValueError:
613	                    continue
614	            db.add(
615	                DocumentFile(
616	                    id=str(uuid4()),
617	                    tree_id=tree.id,
618	                    document_id=document_id,
619	                    kind=row.get("kind", "link"),
620	                    filename=row.get("filename"),
621	                    url=file_url,
622	                    mime_type=file_mime,
623	                    size=file_size,
624	                    created_at=row.get("created_at") or utcnow_iso(),
625	                )
626	            )
627	        progress_cb(87)
628	
629	        _import_links(db, bundle.get("document_member_links", []),
630	                      DocumentMemberLink, "document_id", document_map, member_map)
631	        _import_doc_links(db, bundle.get("event_document_links", []),
632	                          EventDocumentLink, "event_id", event_map, document_map)
633	        _import_doc_links(db, bundle.get("story_document_links", []),
634	                          StoryDocumentLink, "story_id", story_map, document_map)
635	        progress_cb(90)
636	
637	        _enforce_import_quota(db, tree)
638	        user = db.get(User, user_id)
639	        if user is not None:
640	            record_activity(
641	                db, tree_id=tree.id, actor=user, action="create",
642	                target_type="import", target_id=tree.id, target_label=tree.name,
643	            )
644	        db.commit()
645	        if user is not None:
646	            publish_tree_event(db, tree, "activity.entry_added", {"tree_id": tree.id})
647	        return tree.id
648	    except Exception:
649	        db.rollback()
650	        if tree_id:
651	            delete_tree_media(tree_id)
652	        raise
653	    finally:
654	        db.close()

657	def _enforce_import_quota(db: Session, tree: Tree) -> None:
658	    """Reject an over-quota import, rolling back the whole tree + its media.
659	
660	    The bundle is fully written (rows flushed, media on disk) before this runs,
661	    so a single full-usage check enforces the owner's quota; on violation we
662	    undo every inserted row and remove the tree's media directory.
663	    """
664	    tree_id = tree.id
665	    db.flush()
666	    try:
667	        check_full_usage_quota(db, tree)
668	    except QuotaExceeded:
669	        db.rollback()
670	        delete_tree_media(tree_id)
671	        raise

678	def _import_links(db, links, model, parent_key, parent_map, member_map):
679	    # Make sure the parent rows added just before this call are inserted, so the
680	    # link rows that reference them don't violate the foreign key.
681	    db.flush()
682	    model_columns = {column.name for column in model.__table__.columns}
683	    for row in links:
684	        parent_old = row[parent_key]
685	        member_old = row["member_id"]
686	        if parent_old in parent_map and member_old in member_map:
687	            data = {
688	                key: value for key, value in row.items() if key in model_columns
689	            }
690	            data[parent_key] = parent_map[parent_old]
691	            data["member_id"] = member_map[member_old]
692	            db.add(model(**data))
